claims.text: The proposed framework combines DFT+CPA, supercell/SQS local-relaxation corrections, and supervised machine-learning calibration against conductivity measurements.
DFT-based KKR-CPA provides a first-principles, configurationally averaged, single-site description of disordered alloys.
SQS or related supercells are commonly used to represent random multicomponent alloys but become computationally demanding as the number of components and required cell size increase.
Supercell/SQS corrections can account for local atomic relaxations that single-site CPA misses.
Machine-learning calibration against experimental data will improve conductivity-prediction accuracy and generalization across temperature and defect regimes.
The model will predict conductivity for bulk HfNbTaTiZr, both nearly defect-free and containing 1 wt.% oxygen, within ±10% of measurements across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Quantum effects and defect-induced weak localization are significant in HfNbTaTiZr at 0–200 K.
Phonon activation and oxygen-defect scattering dominate conductivity behavior at 300–1200 K.
Oxygen impurities and point defects induce local lattice distortions and may cluster, thereby modifying electron-scattering paths.
At 0 K, compositional disorder in disordered alloys causes electron scattering, with atomic, magnetic, and displacement-disorder contributions.
At low temperature, localization and impurity scattering lower the conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr relative to an ideal crystal.
At high temperature, the framework captures increased phonon scattering and additional defect scattering caused by oxygen.
Existing analytical models typically assume perfect, defect-free crystals and omit defect scattering and oxygen-induced lattice distortion.
Existing analytical models typically deviate by more than 25% from experimental conductivity values.
The hybrid model will improve accuracy from baseline errors greater than 25% to errors no larger than 10%.
A held-out conductivity measurement for the 1 wt.% oxygen specimen at 800 K is expected to be approximately 4.5×10^5 S/m.
A prediction differing by more than 15% from the held-out 800 K benchmark will falsify the hypothesis.
The stated applicability is limited to ambient-pressure, bulk, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr in the two specified temperature ranges.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis claims performance for both nearly defect-free and 1 wt.% oxygen samples across both temperature regimes, whereas the experiment assigns nearly defect-free samples only to 0–200 K and oxygen-containing samples only to 300–1200 K. It therefore does not test the full stated sample-by-temperature applicability.

The accuracy claim is ±10%, but falsification requires an error greater than 15%. Results between 10% and 15% would violate the claimed performance while not meeting the stated falsification criterion.
